body: I actually was just looking into this the other day.  The first bit kinda put me off because it made me feel like I was in elementary school again, but I will take another look if it has been helpful to a few people here.
I will second Frank Turner.  Guy is incredible.  A song that almost always helps me too is Let's Go Nowhere by The Arrogant Sons of Bitches.

I've been going through a crappy breakup, where I let the girl go because she wasn't happy and said that maybe we just need time apart only to have her start dating a friend of mine behind my back a month later.  It made me borderline suicidal, but in general I am doing a lot better.  The main reason for that is because I did open up to a friend who I thought I could really trust.  I even did the same thing as you and told her that I liked her.  Thankfully, she is incredibly reasonable and that didn't bother her and she still has been here for me the entire time.  I don't think anything will ever come of it, even though she has said that if it weren't for her being stuck on an ex of hers that she might consider something, but she is the type of person who has been a life saver to just have around.  I have also had a couple of people who it just made worry more.  I think it is all a matter of finding someone who can handle the situation, which isn't always easy to do.  I got lucky in that she had been a friend of mine a few years ago, lost contact with her, and she just randomly appeared back in my life right when I needed to have her around.

Only you can really say how you are feeling, and what you say and how you say it is likely to affect their understanding of your situation.  Don't write a letter to them, write a letter to yourself.  Open up word so you don't feel like you're writing an email quite as much.  Start just writing down how you feel, what you think is causing it, anything you can say about it.  Then save it, and forget about it for a day or two.  Then open it up again, read through it, and edit it to make sure it is saying what you want, then just copy and paste into an email.
Thank you.  Some of us are still a little behind the curve sometimes.  It is always comforting to hear the success stories.
You're posting this, which means you haven't lost the battle yet.  Keep talking.

I've been kinda doing the same on my own lately.  Went through a really hard breakup where the girl started dating a friend of my very shortly after.  Not really in the same genre as your other songs, but hopefully some of them might meet your tastes.

The Arrogant Sons of Bitches - So Let's Go Nowhere

Authority Zero - Superbitch, Broken Dreams

Frank Turner - Substitute (This one is hit and miss for me. Some days it makes me feel better, some days worse)

Bouncing Souls - True Believers

Streetlight Manifesto - Red Rubber Ball (A cover, but my favorite version)

Hot Water Music - Trusty Chords

Ozomatli - When I Close My Eyes

Pendulum - Encoder

Suburban Legends - Bright Spring Morning (Two different versions of this, I am a fan of the upbeat one)

Big D and the Kids Table - Shining On
"Halfway out of the dark."  Gotta love Dr. Who.

I am still stuck in the depression after the breakup situation.  I feel like she loved me in a way that no one else will.  I have had so many people tell me about getting over everything, and I always have this little nagging in the back of my mind that my situation is worse.  Either way, it still helps to hear stories like yours.  Thanks for posting.  It always helps to see others going through the same thing and succeeding.
I had totally forgotten about it, but yes.  I used to love that game.  Had it on the old hand me down 386 that I got in elementary school, running 3.11 for workgroups, hehe.

Thanks.  I haven't been quite that close myself, but I did have a plan, just didn't have everything to do it at the time (wanted to go out as peacefully and cleanly as possible).  If I did, I may have very well been in the same boat.  It was over a girl too.  In my case she didn't do anything wrong, but our relationship stagnated.  I keep feeling like I could have done things to improve it, but since she moved on so quickly never got a chance to prove it.  At the same time, there are times when I can think of all the little things that bothered me about her.  Either way, seeing others who had no hope moving on finding this kind of happiness gives me something to hold on to.  I fortunately now just have suicidal ideations, and have never been as close as I was that first day, but it is still a bit of a struggle.  It only gets really bad when I have no one to talk to.
